reviews.reviewbody: Superb, many thanks
405-AAA_Track-1.wav begins with Apollo 7 audio. Not 13.

Thanks for contacting about the mission audio files! The Apollo 13 mission tapes are on 7-track, 1/4 inch. The tapes run about six hours apiece. I originally digitized this mission about six years ago, at a time when I didn't have enough parallel processing (and hard drive space) to capture all seven tracks at once. I have that capability now, so I am re-digitizing the original tapes, this time all seven tracks...
Thanks again for the contact! Should have some content here in a few weeks or so...
Cheers~
John

A lot of noise on track 1 (the public release line), but track 3 appears to have the same recording - but without the noise!

I should have checked more recordings before giving a negative review!!!

Definitely five stars!

Colin.

Hi John

I agree that this track is a simulation and it takes place on St Patrick’s Day, March 17th, 1970 as they do reference St Patrick’s Day by name and the crew don’t want to miss their liberty. But from what I gather this simulation is with the Apollo 13 backup crew; CMDR: John W. Young, CMP: John L. "Jack" Swigert and LMP: Charles M. Duke, Jr and not the prime crew. 

At approximately 02 min and 04 sec the audio picks with the debriefing from the simulation and later on someone will mention that the backup crew is on the line ready for the debriefing. At approximately 01 hour and 36 sec into the track the audio picks up toward the beginning of the simulation. 

The Flight Director is Milt Windler which would make this the maroon team and the maroon team EECOM is John Aaron. Throughout the track you will hear the CAPCOM (sounds like Joe Kerwin) call out to the command module simulator as  “Apollo 13” and often refer to the crew by name John, Jack or Charlie.

Track 938-AAG is Apollo 11, Neil and Buzz prepping for their EVA..

Thanks
Larry

First, many many thanks for making this fantastic resource available.

Second: files 03-06-11_Air-to-Ground.zip and 03-07-11_Air-to-Ground.zip contain Shuttle/ISS soundbites. Haven't listened to each and every file inside the archive, but every one I did listen to was Shuttle related.

Third: I had a hard time downloading these files. Many many times the downloads would end in mid-stream, because the server stopped transmitting. I analysed for network problems on my side (I'm an IT engineer...) but I haven't found any. Anyone else had the same experience with downloads from archive.org ?

Fourth: any chance the 4 missing files (as indicated by Mr. Larry's post on 8 March 2012) can/will be added anytime soon?

reviews.reviewbody: Thanks to the laborer who made and uploaded these files. My impression of the astronauts trial seems to be uncommon even, well, Ive never ever heard anyone say it this way. Commander Lovell seemed bitter after the accident. Fred and Rusty seemed a little shocked but functioned well. Now mind I do not blame Jim Lovell, I believe I surley would have turned to self pity at my bad luck. Jim was sarcastic at times, before the biggest obsticles to survival had been licked. I say he was severley disappointed about his situation which means... he hadnt given failure much thought before launch. I would have expected that. Anders said that it was 1/3 they'd make it on the moon, 1/3 they wouldnt make it but get back and 1/3 death. I hold these to be about right given the complexity and newness of almost all of the technology. Those machines must have had some fine engineering in them because they all got back, even Apollo 13. Only because of the quality and the adaptability of the space crafts, did they get back. Charging the CSMs battery was one miracle way above some others. The big lithium canister adaptation was not clever at all but it's all documentaries talk about, how silly. That was a no brainer and the logical next step, a school boy would have figured that out. Above all I think is the skill of those 'Fly Boys'. Threading into the re-entry slot by hand and eye coordination with a burn from the still attached an wobbling  LEM!?!?! This was the greatest of the miracles I think.

Many thanks to John Stoll for uploading these priceless audio tracks.  This collection of Apollo 13 tapes (and all the other missions he has uploaded) are a goldmine of information for people who have a genuine interest in Apollo and the US Space Program.

The printed transcripts help but there are numerous errors in them.  Listening to the voices can not only correct these errors but also give an insight into the emotions going on at the time.  This is especially true of Apollo 13.

For those interested 414-AAA TRACK-3 is the Air To Ground track for before and during the accident.  This also contains the PAO commentary.  I downloaded this track and many others and I can give a few time stamps as follows.  These are given a second or two before the event:

2:51:20 - End of TV broadcast

2:58:24 - CAPCOM gives instruction to stir up Cryo tanks

3:00:20 - Static burst indicating the mishap in the Service Module occured

3:00:44 - Swigert declares they have a problem, which     is repeated by Lovell about 10 seconds later.

787-AAI to 790-AAI is the Flight Loop.  Gene Kranz is the Flight Director at the start and hands over to Glyn Lunney during 788-AAI.

Many thanks again John!  A priceless collection.

So upon playing track 414-AAA TRACK-3 in the embedded player here on the site the correct times (relative to those posted by dave4455) are as follows:

Instruction to stir tanks: 2:32:20
Static burst: 2:33:55
Swigert declares they have a problem: 2:34:25

All times here are given with a few seconds of lead before the noted event occurs.

I need to find some specific lines from the audio recording. I've been using the transcript on space log.org. What is the method for finding them. The timecode and files names don't seem to correspond.
How can i down load a audio file???

reviews.reviewtitle: Why Do I Want to Cry?
reviews.reviewbody:
I hear these playbacks and think back to how so very long ago this era was –– or was it? And it makes me want to cry.  

It seemed that back then there was still much optimism and hope for our future. Things were so different in the country then.  Of course the Watergate scandal then the oil embargo, and on and on occurred and despite it shaking us to the core, it still wasn’t clear that the "good old days" were gone.  

But who would have thought that decades would pass and it would become far worse? 

I can't say how it must feel for those who have lived most of their lives in the more prosperous larger cities in the country, but as far as the smaller locals, times grew hard and never really ever returned to the way they had been before all...  and I mean all our companies abandoned these shores for greater profits overseas.

  Perhaps for the larger cities where economic down turns may not have been so keenly felt, or if they were they didn't last long and were followed by some bounce back, perhaps these things I say may not make sense.  Yet, maybe they may not even seem possible, but most of the nation, its people, and the culture has degraded terribly ever since. It isn’t just our economy, or even our standard of living that has eroded so much (placing us now in 20th place in the world), but our society itself.  It has become crass, selfish, and so darn incohesive.  You hear the comment everywhere that no one cares about anyone as if that is something that just occurred these past ten or twenty years.  No... it began as far back as the 1970s. Of course, this is part of our adopted ideas and mythologies of how we view ourselves as Americans; independent, bootstrap puller-uppers, etc.  No need for anyone, until one needs something... 

But then were we ever truly one “united” nation at all?  Did we ever really see ourselves as “fellow citizens” instead of just American consumers as we were trained to think of ourselves during the Bush, Jr., years?  Throughout those eight years, suddenly you never heard one journalist refer to us as American Citizens anymore. 
 That word "citizen" suddenly vanished from their lips entierly to be replaced by "consumers" no mater what the subject of our being mentioned.  It idid not revert back to citizen until the Obama years... and suddenly so. 

So, I have to ask, did we ever see each other, or even other States other than our own as anything other than strangers? Because now we fear each other as threats, competitors, and nothing more.

So hearing this brings back all those good feelings of hope and optimism despite the social revolution, the slow slide into mass psychosis, and the idea of an “ownership society”, which was just one more euphemism for corporate control or as I had learned decades earlier as being nothing more than fascism. 

We hadn't really fallen from grace yet, and now?  After forty to fifty years, it all seems so dire as to be hopelessly helpless. And I think this is why when I listen to these I feel so sad, that it is all I can do to keep from crying.  Maybe it is my age, and all the decades that have passed, the changes, the advancements, the wars, the corruptions and scandals, and the ever dwindling diminishing of the middle section of the middle class throughout it all, or just my age again… 

Who would have thought that our space program would eventually become one more for profit scenario for corporate interests rather than as it should be; an endeavor by the people, the average man and woman who actually made this country.  It was all done through our work, our educating ourselves, our tax money, and so much more; all put forth in good faith either directly or indirectly.  But how that sensibility has not just changed, it has been all but wiped out entirely in just a few short decades where now many like to glorify the wealthy and their companies as being the backbone of the nation––or as some like to stupidly utter “the makers and the takers” How I have come to detest those words. 

And that too makes the tears well up.  

I remember all the talk and apprehension in 1984 of "big brother" being upon our doorstep the assumption being that it would be our government as in the book. . . when in reality it was a quiet revolution towards fascism.  How we as Americans could ever forget that the one enemy to the average person throughout all of written human history has not been government per se’ but those who always managed to either control it or be it––the top wealth holders.  It has always been that way, the aristocracy… now to be renamed corporatocracy.  Once again, or maybe ever since––they’ve managed to not just gain great influence, but have taken back their long coveted position of control and power over everything.  Government by the people for the people?  Only if you are within the top 8% wealth holders.  

The more things change the more they remain the same. It’s just so sad to see how easily through entertainment orientation, consumerism and materialism, and laziness and entire society can not only be anesthetized into submission, but seem to not care or notice the fantasy of a free people we like to believe ourselves to be.
